title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
prompt: You are given an integer array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a stock on day `i`. On each day you may buy and/or sell the stock, but you can only hold at most one share at a time — you must sell before buying again. Return the maximum total profit achievable across as many transactions as you like.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 1 (price 1), sell on day 2 (price 5), profit = 4. Buy on day 3 (price 3), sell on day 4 (price 6), profit = 3. Total = 7.
Buy on day 0, sell on day 4, profit = 4. Buying and selling every day gives the same total.
Prices only fall, so no transaction is profitable.

hints: With unlimited transactions allowed, you don't need to track specific buy/sell days at all.
Think of the price array as a sequence of rising and falling 'windows' — you only profit from the upward runs.

Every time the price increases from one day to the next, that increase can be captured as profit; summing all positive day-to-day increases gives the same total as the best possible transaction sequence.

solution.approach: Since any number of transactions is allowed and you must sell before buying again, the maximum total profit equals the sum of every positive day-to-day price increase. This works because any profitable multi-day hold can be decomposed into the sum of its daily deltas, and skipping the negative deltas (by selling and rebuying) never costs anything since transactions are free and unlimited. A single pass comparing each day to the previous one suffices.
